_help: Tells the plugin what kind of text a layer is, so the right rules apply (for example, button rules only run on buttons).

Each pattern is a case-insensitive regular expression matched against: the text layer's own name (if it was renamed), its text style name, and the names and variant values of the components it sits inside.
Order matters: when several contexts match, the one listed first wins.
"strong" contexts are controls. If a text layer sits inside one (for example, a Button component), that wins over anything else.
"parent" means a context also gets every rule for its parent (a text-only button follows all button rules, except the length limit).
Text that matches nothing is treated as body text. After editing, run: node figma-plugin/build.mjs

"ignore" lists fonts and text styles that draw icons from words (like "chevron-up" or "wallet"). Text in them is skipped. Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the font family and the text style name.
What counts as a link, besides a real Figma hyperlink or an underline.
textStyles: text style names. colorNames: color style or color variable names applied to the text.
blueText: treat any blue text color as a link. colors: exact link colors (hex) to also accept.

textOnlyButtons._help: How the plugin tells text-only buttons (up to 5 words) from buttons with a container (3 words). A button counts as text-only if one of its variant values matches these patterns, or if the button has no visible background or border.
